messages:
ashley: FYI saw a weird burst where a subset of clients dropped SSE then opened WS and both paths accepted the same resume token -> double billing and duplicate responses in UI. observed in na-central after canary.
tom: ugh. did they keep the same session id on both?
ashley: yes, client lib falls back to ws and reuses session_id+resume. proxy logs show two different backends accepted concurrently for ~12s.
zara: paste logs?
ashley: snippet:
```
[2025-06-12T09:21:03Z] conn=sse-7a state=STREAM_OPEN session=su:567 accept=ok route=na-central-1
[2025-06-12T09:21:04Z] conn=ws-c9 state=WS_OPEN session=su:567 accept=ok route=na-central-2
[2025-06-12T09:21:15Z] billing: session=su:567 resume=true tokens=+1 route=na-central-1
[2025-06-12T09:21:16Z] billing: session=su:567 resume=true tokens=+1 route=na-central-2
```
infra-bot: ALERT: duplicate-session-detector triggered 2025-06-12T09:21:20Z count=18 window=5m
tom: that implies our acceptance is per-connection and there's no cross-proxy claim. We should have an acceptance lease in central metastore to prevent dual-accept.
azara: iirc we debated central lease vs eventual reconcile last Q. central lease adds sync traffic on accept path though.
analytics: telemetry shows spike on "duplicate_response_rate" + UI flicker metrics for chat windows. correlated with a feature flag roll that enabled ws fallback.
product-luis: users saw duplicated assistant messages and were charged twice. need a quick mitigation and a long-term fix.
ashley: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) prevent protocol fallback in the SDK during rollout for 48h, 2) make proxy accept idempotent by checking kvcache and rejecting if another route has an active lease within TTL.
tom: 2) sounds safer for clients. We can add a lightweight accept-check RPC to control plane: on accept, route does compare-and-set session -> owner=routeX ttl=30s. If fails, reject accept and instruct client to reconnect after jitter.
azara: that requires client to handle a new error code ACCEPTED_ELSEWHERE and backoff. SDK changes take time.
product-luis: can we return a transparent UI reason so customers know it was a transient dup? need to reduce support.
analytics: console change request: add a new column in streaming sessions table: "live_claim_owner" and a legend explaining acceptance lease TTL. Also add alert for "session_claim_conflicts" when >5 in 5m.
console-bot: NOTE: created draft dashboard /dashboards/streaming/claim-conflicts and ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-STREAM-2201
tom: long-term: central acceptance registry + route cookie approach (route cookie issued after handshake) so clients always reconnect to the same route. Pro: fewer cross-accept races. Con: adds handshake RTT and statefulness.
azara: alternative: make resume tokens carry an "accept-nonce" signed by control-plane that increments on each accept. If route sees a later nonce accepted elsewhere, it must drop its session and instruct client to rejoin a single owner. That still needs central sequencing but could be sharded.
ashley: another edge: SSE -> WS fallback crosses protocol layers, some proxies don't map client IP consistently so route affinity by cookie may fail. we should prefer server-side claim model that is identity-first (session id + account id) not relying on client affinity.
tom: agree. Implementation plan: 1) implement optimistic accept-check RPC to control plane (fast-path cache + compare-and-set) 2) add SDK handling for ACCEPTED_ELSEWHERE 3) console telemetry and billing dedupe logic to detect and merge double-charges within 2m window.
product-luis: priority?
analytics: telemetry and console changes can be done in 2 sprints. infra accept-check proto: 3 sprints including canary. SDK changes: 2 sprints. Billing dedupe: ops/legal must sign off but we can instrument quickly to surface suspected duplicates.
azara: for canary, we'll enable accept-check for na-central-1 only, and keep ws-fallback flag off for canary cohort.
ashley: temporary rollback: disabling ws fallback globally would stop new dup incidents but we have customers relying on fallback for bad networks. prefer targeted canary + accept-check.
console-bot: DEPLOY NOTE: feature-flag ws-fallback toggled to off for 10% of traffic at 2025-06-12T09:35:00Z by infra-bot.
tom: need to write runbook update: how to interpret "claim conflict" in console and steps (kick session owner -> force route reconcilation). I'll draft.
product-luis: I'll prep support FAQ and a small in-console banner for affected customers explaining duplicated messages and a credit timeline.
ashley: filed tasks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-10234 (accept-check RPC), https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SDK-887 (ACCEPTED_ELSEWHERE handling), https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-503 (dedupe instrumentation).
analytics: we'll add event names: "session_claim_attempt", "session_claim_result", "session_claim_conflict_reason" to the telemetry schema.
azara: ok let's prioritise infra-10234 and console dashboard. Anyone object?
product-luis: no objections. roll forward.
ashley: rolling a small canary for accept-check on na-central-1 in 10m. will monitor duplicate_response_rate and billing probabilities.
infra-bot: CANARY: accept-check service rolled to na-central-1 (10% traffic) at 2025-06-12T09:45:00Z by ashley.
